layer: Tax on the act of converting
note: No tax on exchanging RMB for dollars appears in the PRC foreign exchange rules read; current payments are unrestricted when the transaction is real and lawful. This is a none-found result, not a legal opinion (flag F07).

layer: PRC income tax on the income behind the balance
amount: 3%–45% wages · 5%–35% business · 20% dividends, rent, asset sales
note: This is the real tax. If it was already withheld, as with payroll, converting adds nothing; the bank only wants the proof. If it was never paid, it is owed whether or not you convert.

layer: PRC tax on bank interest earned on the balance
note: Savings deposit interest has been exempt since 9 October 2008.

layer: Tax recordal for one payment above USD 50,000
note: A form filed with the tax office for listed payment types, which include a foreign individual's pay for work in China, dividends and proceeds from selling real estate. Whether the bank wants it from you is for the bank to confirm (flag F14).

amount: 0.21% at Bank of China when read
note: Half the gap between the bank's posted buying and selling rates: RMB 0.01405 per dollar.

amount: RMB 200 to 410 per wire at Bank of China
note: 0.1% with a RMB 50 floor and RMB 260 cap, plus RMB 150 cable. Fees taken by intermediary and receiving banks are not published and are left blank (flag F02).

layer: U.S. income tax on the underlying income
note: A U.S. citizen owes U.S. tax on worldwide income in the year it is earned, not when it is moved. PRC income tax on the same income can be credited on Form 1116; qualifying earned income up to USD 132,900 for 2026 can be excluded instead, but tax on excluded income cannot also be credited.

If the RMB is worth more dollars when converted than when you received it, the difference is a gain. The yuan is stronger today than the 2023 to 2025 averages, so this can be the largest U.S. cost; see the worked table below.

amount: No tax; up to USD 16,536 if missed non-wilfully
note: Due when foreign accounts together passed USD 10,000 at any time in the year. The wilful dollar maximum in the table is USD 165,353.
Thresholds start at USD 50,000 for a single filer living in the U.S. and USD 200,000 living abroad. Up to USD 50,000 more after an IRS notice, and 40% on related understatements.

amount: No tax to the recipient; penalties if missed
note: Needed when gifts or bequests from one foreign person and related persons pass USD 100,000 in the year.

amount: No charge; seizure risk if not declared
note: More than USD 10,000 in currency must be reported on FinCEN Form 105.

layer: Catching up on missed U.S. filings
amount: 5% of the highest balance if you live in the U.S.; no penalty if you qualify as living abroad
note: For non-wilful cases only. The domestic procedure charges 5% of the highest year-end balance; the foreign procedure charges tax and interest but no penalty. Whether you qualify is a personal fact (flag F09).
Applies to evasion, fraudulent purchase and private FX trading; SAFE has applied the evasion article to splitting cases. Unlawful carrying of cash: up to 20%.
